# NASA outlay data in millions from FY 2008-2017
nasa_outlays = {
    2008: 17834,
    2009: 19168,
    2010: 18906,
    2011: 17617,
    2012: 17190,
    2013: 16978,
    2014: 17093,
    2015: 18272,
    2016: 18828,
    2017: 18698
}

# Convert to billions
values = [v/1000 for v in nasa_outlays.values()]
print("NASA outlays (billions):")
for year, val in zip(sorted(nasa_outlays.keys()), values):
    print(f"  {year}: {val:.3f}")

# Sort values for Winsorization
sorted_values = sorted(values)
print(f"\nSorted values: {sorted_values}")

# 10% Winsorized: For n=10, 10% of 10 = 1 value
# Replace min with 2nd smallest, max with 2nd largest
winsorized = sorted_values.copy()
winsorized[0] = winsorized[1]  # Replace min with 2nd smallest
winsorized[-1] = winsorized[-2]  # Replace max with 2nd largest

print(f"Winsorized values: {winsorized}")

# Calculate 10% Winsorized mean
winsorized_mean = sum(winsorized) / len(winsorized)
print(f"\n10% Winsorized mean: {winsorized_mean:.4f} billion")

# The range is max - min after Winsorization
winsorized_range = winsorized[-1] - winsorized[0]

# Another interpretation: what are the bounds (the min and max after Winsorization)
print(f"\nWinsorized bounds: min = {winsorized[0]:.4f}, max = {winsorized[-1]:.4f}")

# The question asks for the "10% Winsorized range"
# Typically this is max - min after Winsorization
print(f"\nFinal answer (10% Winsorized range): {winsorized_range:.2f} billion")

import numpy as np

# NASA outlay data in millions from FY 2008-2017

print("Winsorized max:", np.max(winsorized))

# 10% Winsorized range = max - min
winsorized_range = np.max(winsorized) - np.min(winsorized)
print(f"\n10% Winsorized range: {winsorized_range:.4f} billion")
